text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Monday morning newspapers:

- Slovenian and Croatian officials said the relations between their two countries had improved since the new Slovenian government, elected last month, pledged to work on improving relations with Croatia as one of its primary goals.
-Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi is expected to arrive for his first official visit to Slovenia on Monday evening.
- Slovenian minority representatives kept an unchanged number of seats in communities in Austria's southern province of Carinthia in local elections on Sunday.
- United List of Social Democrats, the former communists, are expected to elect new party leadership during a congress in Ljubljana next weekend.

- The Christian Democratic Party said it would look into the reasons for its poor showing in November's general election when it won just ten parliamentary seats, down from 15 four years ago. However, the party said it would not replace its current leader Lozje Peterle.
